correctness.rationale: For radial parametrization x(θ)=r(θ)e_θ, Lipschitz r>0 and q=sqrt(r²+(r′)²), boundary arclength density q/P. A segment passing arbitrarily near the origin must have nearly antipodal endpoint angles; central symmetry makes second radius r(θ+δ) and q periodic by π. Its exact distance ab|sin δ|/sqrt(a²+b²+2ab cos δ) is r(θ)|δ|/2+O_K(δ²) uniformly, and for sufficiently small |δ| the foot lies inside the finite segment. Thus the allowed second-angle interval has width 4ε/r(θ)+O_K(ε²); Lebesgue differentiation and dominated convergence yield κ=4/P²∫q²/r. Subtract 4/P=4/P²∫q to find exact deficit (4/P²)∫(r′²/r) q/(q+r). Since 1/2≤q/(q+r)<1 where r′ finite, obtain sharp coefficient 2/P² and rigidity r′=0 a.e. A strictly convex perturbation r=1+η cos2θ makes q/(q+r)→1/2 uniformly where r′≠0, proving optimality of constant 2. Square has r=secθ on each side, q=sec²θ, κ=4/64×4∫_{−π/4}^{π/4}sec³θ dθ=(√2+log(1+√2))/4. Independently evaluated this integral and a separate opposite-side endpoint-coordinate Jacobian. Finite simulations in source are not used as proof.
